title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore West on 1969-12-07
source: Source: sbd > Bear's cassette master  (probably) > dat (Rob Eaton) > dat (44k) - Provided by Tim Dalton; Transfer: Dat > Sony PCM-R500 > Tascam DA-3000 > wav 16/44.1 - Transferred by Charlie Miller; Lineage: wav 16/44.1 > iZotope RX6 Advanced > iZotope Ozone 5 Advanced > CD Wave >Flac16; edited and mastered SIRMick

ai_review.summary: Soundboard recording with slight hiss captures a powerful single‑set show featuring standout jams on Black Peter, Dancin', The Eleven > Love Light and Pigpen’s top‑form blues numbers.
ai_review.review: The performance is praised for its raw energy and tight segues – highlights include the rare Black Peter opener, a Dark‑Star‑like jam in Dancin’, and the primal Eleven→Love Light sequence. The soundboard source is generally clear despite a brief hiss at the beginning, making the show enjoyable for fans who appreciate 1969 Dead intensity.

ai_rating.rationale: Reviews overwhelmingly highlight strong musical moments and only note minor hiss in the recording; weighted average of show (≈4.5) and recording (≈4.0) yields a solid 4.3 rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Slight hiss at the start of the Black Peter opener, but overall a clear and well‑balanced mix with no major dropouts.

show_quality.setlist_flow: A single‑set show that weaves blues numbers and jam sequences together; transitions such as Mama Tried→Easy Wind and The St. Stephen→The Eleven→Love Light are highlighted for their fluidity.

band_member_comments.Jerry: His guitar shines, especially the Dark‑Star‑like solo in Dancin' and the opening of The Eleven > Love Light.
band_member_comments.Bob: Weir’s vocal performance on Mama Tried receives special mention.
band_member_comments.Keys: Tom Constanten’s organ adds melodic texture, noted as a highlight of the set.
